walkthrough: Day 1, 0-15 min: 5-step form. Company step fine. 'Problem category' dropdown: 'capacity expansion' maybe. The goal suggestions feel generic, but I type my own. Review, submit.
Day 1, 15-25 min: data page table. I click 'Someone else has this' on ERP production, cost and sales items and invite my analyst. The pending/done state is good because I can see what he hasn't done.
Day 1: I log out. The analyst uploads that evening. 'We read 48,000 rows, Jan 2023-Dec 2025' is the first thing that makes me trust it a little.

Day 2: the CEO says the board also wants acquiring a competitor compared. I open the dashboard. No obvious place to change the goal. Is the form locked after submission? Do I have to re-run the 5-step form or start a new engagement? STUCK 1.

Day 2: I fall back to the 'messages' tile and type the change. No sign whether the scope, data items, price or turnaround changed. STUCK 2: does the acquisition need competitor financials I don't have? The table doesn't update until someone acts.
Days 2-5: dashboard says 'analysis 40%'. 40% of what? 'Early charts' before anything has been checked: I would screenshot them and ask my analyst where the numbers came from. Suspicious. STUCK 3.
Day 6-8: the formal report has sources and ASSUMPTION tags, and Strong/Weak ratings. That part is good. But I'm not sure the acquisition option was really analysed or just bolted on.
Abandon risk: day 2. If the change needs a new engagement and a new invoice, I'd email the consultant directly instead.
Y.quote: Progress bars and early charts are what vendors show you to look busy. And the minute my board changed the question, the form had nowhere to put it.

walkthrough: Day 1, 0-10 min: one text box: 'Should we open a second plant in the GCC, capex ~X, demand outlook?'. 4 follow-up questions on the same page. Fast, no chatbot. Good.
Day 1: 'What we understood' lines. I correct one: the hurdle rate is 12%, not 10%. Being able to edit their understanding line by line is exactly what I want.
Day 1: next-step card: 'Invite your analyst to upload ERP cost data, owner: Rashid, ~30 min'. I invite him. Clear.

Day 2: the board asks for the acquisition option. I go to 'What we understood' and edit/add a line: 'Also compare acquiring competitor Y as an alternative'. Easy to type. But is it now 'Understand' again? Does the tracker go back a stage? Does the data checklist get new items, e.g. target financials or a valuation? Nothing tells me what the edit triggers. STUCK 1.

Day 2-3: if the checklist grows with 'Competitor financials (Helpful)' and 'We don't have it → what happens instead' (e.g. using public filings as an assumption), that's acceptable. I need to see the new delivery date and whether there's an extra charge. STUCK 2: not shown.
Days 3-7: the tracker in words says 'Checking'. Better than a %. Waiting states with an expected date are fine.
Day 8: the report moves to the top: plant vs acquisition vs do nothing, each number sourced or marked ASSUMPTION. I [Ask a question] on the acquisition synergy figure.
Abandon risk: low. Mild risk on day 2 if editing a line silently does nothing.
X.quote: I can edit what they think my problem is. That's the right idea. Just tell me what my edit costs me in days and dirhams.

walkthrough: Day 1, 0-10 min: starts as texting. Honestly, my first reaction is 'another chatbot'. I give terse answers. The follow-ups are reasonable. 8 minutes.
Day 1: the page appears with 'What we understood'. I check it like a term sheet and fix the hurdle rate. Next-step card: invite the analyst. Done.
Day 1 evening: the analyst uploads ERP data. The row/period confirmation appears.

Day 2: the CEO's request. I open the side panel: 'Board also wants acquiring a competitor compared to the second plant.' The consultant replies and proposes changes to 'What we understood', plus new data items (target financials, integration costs). I see the page change. That is the easiest reframe of the four, about 5 minutes.

Day 2: STUCK 1. Does the widened scope go back to the consultant for approval before work continues? Does the timeline move? I need the new date and any fee change stated in the panel answer, on the record.

Day 2-3: suspicion: 'answers can turn into page changes'. Who changed what? I want a visible change log: 'Scope changed day 2 at CFO request'. Otherwise in 3 months nobody can prove the board asked for it. STUCK 2.
Days 3-8: I use the panel: 'why do you need integration cost estimates?'. A good answer. The report compares plant vs acquisition with sources and confidence. I ask about one Weak finding.
Abandon risk: only in the first 10 minutes, if the chat feels like a toy. After that, low.
Z.quote: I didn't want to text a bot, but when the board moved the goalposts, I could just say so, and the page actually changed. Show me the audit trail of that change and you have me.

walkthrough: Day 1, 0-15 min: one conversation. Questions one at a time. It works, but it's slow, and I can't see the whole picture.
Day 1: the 'What we understood' summary arrives as a message. To correct it I have to reply in text. Was my correction applied? I scroll up to check. STUCK 1.
Day 1: a data item message with 'invite' for the analyst. Fine. The analyst gets a data-only login, so he doesn't read my conversation. Good.

Day 2: reframing is trivially easy to type: 'board also wants acquisition compared'. The consultant acknowledges it. But the original understanding summary is now 40 messages up, and there's no single current version of the scope. STUCK 2.
Days 3-7: I type 'what do you still need?' to get a list. I should not have to ask. Waiting updates get buried among messages.
Day 8: the report arrives as a message. Export to PDF/Word is what I'd actually use. Tracing which version of the goal the report answers means scrolling back. STUCK 3.
Abandon risk: medium. It feels like a WhatsApp group with a vendor. I would ask for a call instead.
W.quote: Easy to tell it the goal changed. Impossible to prove later what the goal was. A CFO can't sign off on a chat log.

change_in_favourite: Z: (1) Let me skip the chat start and type the problem in one box (X's start); chat optional. (2) Any scope change from the side panel creates a visible, dated 'Scope change' entry on the page: old goal, new goal, who asked, new data items, new delivery date and fee impact. I confirm it explicitly before work restarts, and it goes to the approver as a framing re-approval. (3) The report states which scope version it answers and includes a 'do nothing' baseline beside both options.
